title: Wave 13 — Register classification from audio: the measured floor
verifier_note: Single-lane deepen on register classification. findings.authors: Boratto, Costa, Meireles, Alves, Saporetti, Bodini, Cury, Goliatt
findings.title: Machine Learning with Evolutionary Parameter Tuning for Singing Registers Classification
findings.finding: On a purpose-built dataset of 350 audio files spanning chest, mixed and head registers, 14 temporal features extracted with the TSFEL Python library fed three ML models whose hyperparameters were tuned by a Differential Evolution algorithm; the DE-optimised Extreme Gradient Boosting model reached an average classification accuracy of 97.60%. Signals 6(1) article 9, published 21 February 2025, open access under CC BY 4.0.
findings.implication: Register classification from audio alone is not an open problem to be routed around — it is a published result whose front end is engineered temporal features, not a neural embedding. A practice tool can gate on register from audio without a sensor. The caveats are the corpus (350 files, internally constructed, voice type and genre unstated in the abstract) and the label provenance, not the method.

sources.claim: Crossref returns exact title, eight authors led by Boratto Tales, Signals 6(1) art. 9, issued 2025-02-21, license CC BY 4.0; the abstract states 350 audio files, TSFEL, 14 temporal features, DE-optimised XGBoost, 97.60% average accuracy.

findings.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Vocal Register Classification in Contemporary Male Pop Music
findings.finding: Full text (v2): 1008 three-second lead-vocal clips, stem-split from pop songs in Logic Pro, were rendered to mel-spectrograms producing 7221 initial images before splitting and augmentation — v1 states 4221 images for the same clip count. Four classes are indexed 0 chest / 1 mix / 2 head mix / 3 head. Augmentation was a horizontal flip plus two brightness variants; the split was 80/20. The SVM reached 0.94 overall accuracy on the test set with per-class metrics spanning 0.91–0.99; the CNN trained for six epochs (68.0% validation accuracy after epoch one). Register labels were assigned by ear from vocal-technique texts (Peckham 2010), not by EGG or laryngoscopy. The authors ship a tool, AVRA (Automatic Vocal Register Analysis). CC BY 4.0.
findings.implication: Wave 8 recorded this paper's four-class scheme but no performance; the measured floor is SVM 0.94 on held-out male pop. Two limits travel with that number. The ground truth is pedagogical annotation, so the classifier reproduces trained listeners' labels and inherits their disagreements — accuracy here is agreement with annotators, never laryngeal state. And the corpus is one genre, one voice type. Reuse the four-class scheme (splitting mix into mix / head-mix is load-bearing near the passaggio) and treat 0.94 as an in-domain ceiling. The v1/v2 image-count discrepancy means the version must be cited, not just the identifier.

sources.claim: Full text v2 §3.1: 'A total of 1008 audio clips were rendered into mel-spectrograms which produced 7221 initial images before splitting and augmentation'; class indices 0–3 chest/mix/head mix/head; SVM test accuracy 0.94 with class metrics 0.91–0.99; six CNN epochs, 68.0% validation accuracy after epoch one; labels from Peckham 2010.
v1 of the same paper states 4221 initial images for the same 1008 clips — the figure changed between versions, so the version must be cited.

lanes.licence_notes: Both sources are CC BY 4.0 — Boratto et al. via the MDPI Signals Crossref license field, Kim & Botha via the arXiv licence on 2505.11378. Text and figures are reusable with attribution. Neither paper releases its dataset, and neither underlying corpus is reusable: Kim & Botha's clips are stem-separated commercial pop recordings.
lanes.gaps: No published replication validating audio-only register classifiers against physiological ground truth (EGG or laryngoscopy) was found anywhere in the 2024–2026 record. Both studies here label by ear from pedagogy texts, so reported accuracy measures agreement with trained annotators, not laryngeal state — the two are not interchangeable, and no located paper quantifies the gap between them. Coverage is narrow: Boratto does not state voice type or genre in the abstract; Kim & Botha is male pop only. No located study measures cross-genre or cross-sex transfer.
